system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Preliminary flag:** The Seller's preamble asserts the draft was "settled at principal level by both deal teams" and is "FINAL and not intended to be re-opened." Our playbook records **no written authority from Amelia Frost** for any fallback position (20% cap, 18-month period, post-completion Riverlark release). Treat the preamble as advocacy, not an agreed record. Every item below should be marked up as OPEN. Recommend we ask Seller counsel to identify the specific principal-level communication they are relying on.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- Seller: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- Buyer wants: 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- Recommendation: **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m.** 20% is our conditional fallback only, and no Amelia Frost authority identifying this draft exists.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- Seller: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only ("deductible") recovery (cl 12.2).
- Buyer wants: de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar ("tipping") recovery once exceeded.
- Recommendation: **Reject on all three elements.** Seller's thresholds are 5x ours and the deductible structure permanently forfeits the first AUD 250,000 of loss.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- Seller: 18 months (cl 12.3/13), plus a default rule that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly carved out.
- Buyer wants: 24 months; limitations apply only where expressly stated.
- Recommendation: **Reject; counter at 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.** 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost approval (none given), and the default rule would silently import general limits into Title/Tax/IP/indemnity regimes.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- Seller: capacity and title warranties subject to same caps/time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- Buyer wants: separate regime – 100% of price cap, minimum 6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Recommendation: **Reject outright.** Folding title into a 20% / 18-month regime would leave us unable to recover the price if we don't actually get the shares.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- Seller: limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5); no fraud carve-out appears anywhere.
- Buyer wants: fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance.
- Recommendation: **Insist on express carve-out; non-negotiable.** Absence of a fraud carve-out is unacceptable and likely unenforceable anyway, but we must not rely on that.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- Seller: general disclosure of entire data room as at 22 Sept 2026, Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Sch 7; DL [1.1]–[1.2]).
- Buyer wants: specific, fair disclosure only; no whole-data-room, public-register or deemed-disclosure.
- Recommendation: **Reject DL [1.1]–[1.2]; require specific disclosures against identified warranties with a "fair disclosure" standard.** General data-room disclosure effectively neutralises the warranty package.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- Seller: no claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- Buyer wants: delete blanket exclusion; any qualifier limited to actual knowledge of named Buyer individuals, and never applying to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. Seller knowledge qualifiers to name seller persons + reasonable enquiry.
- Recommendation: **Delete cl 8.3.** A "discoverable" standard imputes constructive knowledge of the whole data room and duplicates the general-disclosure problem in SPA-N-006.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- Seller: reasonable endeavours; consent deemed satisfied on delivery of written consent (cl 3/6.3). DL [2] confirms no final consent and no evidence of cl 11.3 conditions in the data room.
- Buyer wants: effective consent AND documentary evidence the 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a condition precedent; not consent-on-delivery; stronger than reasonable endeavours.
- Recommendation: **Reject; make effective, unconditional (or condition-satisfied) Bluefen consent a CP.** This is ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m) with an express change-control clause; "delivery of a letter" is not the same as a satisfied consent.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- Seller: ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2/7). DL [3] confirms not repaid, no discharge in data room.
- Buyer wants: current payout letter, repayment direct from Completion funds, and effective security releases delivered at Completion. Post-completion release only with irrevocable bank undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- Recommendation: **Reject post-completion release; require payout letter and deed of release/PPSR discharge as Completion deliverables.** Debt-free/cash-free is meaningless if we complete with AUD 3.2m of secured debt still outstanding.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- Seller: DD-005 AUD 420,000 closing bonuses "a matter for the Seller," not itemised in funds flow. DL [5] confirms exclusion from funds flow and silence on on-costs.
- Buyer wants: AUD 420,000 plus triggered payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or demonstrably Seller-funded (price deduction or Seller direct payment).
- Recommendation: **Require express treatment in funds flow and SPA (Seller-borne, grossed up for on-costs).** If silent, the Company (i.e. the Buyer) pays these post-Completion.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- Seller: indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). DL [4] confirms cl 7.3 transfer is conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee, AUD 180,000 open per DD-010 (not bank-verified), no receipt or confirmatory assignment in data room.
- Buyer wants: broader indemnity covering title/ownership of the SOW3 Project Materials, third-party claims, and costs of perfecting the assignment; preserve the cure (pay/obtain confirmatory assignment pre-Completion).
- Recommendation: **Broaden the indemnity and require pre-Completion cure where possible (payment receipt + confirmatory assignment).** Do not treat the AUD 180,000 as verified either way; the exposure is loss of IP, not just a fee.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- Seller: "preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Sch 6). DL [6] confirms ~1,240 records, unknown access/scope, notification status undetermined, no loss stated.
- Buyer wants: log preservation, documented investigation, pre-Completion updates, warranty/indemnity cover for regulatory/notification costs if a breach is later confirmed. Do not assume confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or any numeric exposure.
- Recommendation: **Require covenant to preserve logs, investigate and update before Completion, plus a specific indemnity for consequences of the DD-006 incident.** Not material today, but the facts are unresolved and the Seller's characterisation is not evidence.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)**
- Seller: ordinary-course operating costs. DL [8] does not state whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course.
- Buyer wants: diligence on timing/scope (DD-008 + DD-011 together); no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Recommendation: **Assess, don't adjust yet.** Seek confirmation of terms; if any renewal is accrued-but-unpaid or non-ordinary-course it moves to working capital/Debt, otherwise accept.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- Seller: all Claims subject to general regime unless expressly stated; Tax/IP "settled under the general regime" (cl 12.3/13; Tax/IP paragraph).
- Buyer wants: Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations and covenant claims each with their own regime; no hidden override.
- Recommendation: **Reject the default-override drafting; insert express schedule of regimes by category.** Otherwise the 20%/18-month limits capture Tax, IP and indemnities by default.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- Seller: title evidenced by Company share register at DD-012. DL [10] concedes this is the "source relied on" and Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- Buyer wants: independent evidence – ASIC extract, share certificates, officer/board authorities, PPSR and encumbrance searches, confirmation no options/convertibles.
- Recommendation: **Treat DD-012 as insufficient; complete independent title DD before signing.** An internal register supplied by the Seller is not independent proof of unencumbered 100% ownership.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- Seller: considered settled under general regime.
- Buyer wants: terms remain OPEN; separate Tax and IP regimes to be negotiated (no unlimited liability assumed, no resolution assumed).
- Recommendation: **Mark as OPEN and reject the "settled" characterisation.** Nothing in our record supports agreement, and folding Tax/IP into the general cap compounds SPA-N-014.

---

**Suggested next steps:** (1) Respond that the draft is not agreed and request the basis for the "FINAL/principal-level" claim; (2) issue a full mark-up on the above; (3) confirm with Amelia Frost that no fallback authority has been or will be given before the mark-up goes out; (4) prioritise the Completion-mechanics items (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, title) as they affect what we actually receive on the day, independent of the liability package.
=== END ADVICE ===
